facts.claim: Sabah keeps its own immigration control under the Malaysia Agreement 1963, so travellers arriving from Peninsular Malaysia go through an immigration check at Kota Kinabalu even on domestic flights.

facts.notes: In 2022 Sabah minister Masidi Manjun said the special immigration requirements, part of MA63, would not be scrapped.

gaps: METHOD: direct access to airports.malaysiaairports.com.my and www.malaysiaairports.com.my was blocked (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND) at the start and again just before finishing, so NO fact in this file is evidence=direct. All 'search' facts come from WebSearch result summaries; the underlying pages were not opened.

METHOD: the shared WebSearch budget for this workflow turn was exhausted after 15 queries. Planned searches for taxi coupon fares, e-hailing pick-up point, car rental, accessibility services, dining/retail outlets, the MAHB careline and terminal operating hours could not be run.
Terminal operating hours (whether Terminal 1 is open 24 hours) - not found; CAAM AD 2.3 hours text not returned.
Distance from the airport to Kota Kinabalu city centre - only background knowledge (about 8 km); not confirmed in this run.
Full-year 2025 passenger total for BKI - not found (only a monthly figure of about 802,000 and the 2024 total).
Official level-by-level terminal directory, number of check-in counters, gates and aerobridges - not verified.

Current domestic airline list (Malaysia Airlines, AirAsia, Batik Air, Firefly, AirBorneo/ex-MASwings) and city-level domestic and international destination list - not verified against an official source.

Whether Batik Air's Kota Kinabalu-Singapore route actually launched in February 2026, whether the Kota Kinabalu-Jeddah route launched, and the true status of AirAsia's Sibu/Bintulu routes (conflicting reports).
Lounges: the current lounge line-up, names (Travel Club Lounge? Golden Lounge?), exact locations, walk-in prices and access rules. Plaza Premium and Golden Lounge status conflict between sources.

Accessibility services: nothing sourced. A third-party guide in a search summary mentions ramps, lifts and accessible toilets but could not be attributed to a URL; wheelchair assistance, accessible parking/drop-off, and any MAHB sensory or hidden-disability provision at BKI are unverified.
Facilities: prayer rooms (surau), baby-care rooms, Wi-Fi, ATMs, money changers, medical clinic, showers, left-luggage prices and hours - not verified.
Dining and retail: no individual outlet names could be sourced; only the generic CAAM statement that shops and cafeterias exist.
Hotels at or near the airport - not researched (search budget).
Taxi: coupon counter location and fares (a city-centre fare of about RM30 is recalled from background knowledge only), night surcharge - not verified.
E-hailing (Grab etc.): designated pick-up point at Terminal 1 and typical fares - not verified.
Car rental: companies with counters at the arrival hall - not verified.

Airport bus: status in 2026 of the legacy RM5 'Airport Bus' to the city centre (Padang Merdeka) is unconfirmed; location of the BAS.MY stop at Terminal 1, official S07/S08 timetable from the airport stop and the official operator fare table were not seen.
Parking: official MAHB rate table, motorcycle rates, lost-ticket fee, accepted cashless payment methods, premium/covered parking and EV charging - not verified (rates come from third-party listings).
Contacts: MAHB customer-care line, lost and found, airport police, immigration and customs office numbers at KKIA - not found; only the CAAM-published operator phone and e-mail.

Immigration: official Sabah Immigration wording for Sarawakians entering Sabah, for children (MyKid/birth certificate), for foreign nationals arriving on domestic flights, and whether autogates/e-gates are available at KKIA - not retrieved from an official page.

Expansion: construction start date, any 2026 works inside Terminal 1 affecting passengers, and an RM11.8 million amenities upgrade mentioned in a search summary (source and date unclear) - not verified.
